claims.text: The initial Al0.7CoCrFeNi alloy is eutectic and has a dual-phase lamellar FCC/B2 microstructure.
The initial alloy combines high strength with brittleness.
Brittleness in the initial alloy is caused by stress concentration at incoherent FCC/B2 interfaces.
HPHT treatment at approximately 6 GPa and 1473 K for 2 hours will transform the lamellar microstructure into a hierarchical pattern.
The HPHT treatment will replace incoherent lamellar interfaces with coherent interfaces.
A hexahedron-anvil apparatus can apply the specified HPHT treatment to this alloy.
Coherent interfaces facilitate dislocation transfer between the FCC and B2 phases.
The hierarchical coherent microstructure enables dislocation transfer, stacking-fault formation, and twinning.
These deformation mechanisms produce a more homogeneous strain distribution.
Homogeneous strain distribution alleviates interfacial stress concentration and arrests interfacial cracking.
The HPHT-induced structure will enhance ductility without a significant loss of strength.
The treated alloy will exhibit elongated crack propagation rather than isolated microcracks.
At high strain, the GND densities of the FCC and B2 phases will converge in the HPHT-treated alloy.
The as-cast Al0.7CoCrFeNi baseline has a fracture strength of approximately 944 MPa and elongation of approximately 25.6%.
The as-cast baseline has a lamellar FCC/B2 structure.
There is a pressure-temperature window that induces the desired topology without causing phase decomposition or instability.
The specified 6 GPa, 1473 K, 2-hour treatment lies within that processing window.
Conventional thermomechanical treatment can alter the strength and ductility of a lamellar FCC/B2 eutectic high-entropy alloy.

contradictions.description: The query specifies a homogenized starting alloy, whereas the baseline is defined as an as-cast alloy; these are distinct material states unless the relationship between them is explained.

The initial material is characterized as brittle, while the baseline assigns it about 25.6% tensile elongation and the cited source characterizes the corresponding, compositionally different alloy as having high ductility. The meaning and test conditions of 'brittle' are not reconciled.
